content: Ferrous sulfate is an essential mineral that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of iron deficiency and iron deficiency anemia. It is used as an iron supplement when a physician determines the need for such therapy. For adults and children aged 12 years and older, the recommended dosage is one tablet daily or as directed by a physician. For children under 12 years of age, consultation with a physician is required to determine appropriate use and dosage. There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of ferrous sulfate in both adult and pediatric patients, whether supported by guidelines or not. Similarly, there is limited information on contraindications for pediatric patients. Warnings include the following: Do not exceed the recommended dosage. Treatment of any anemic condition should be conducted under the advice and supervision of a physician. Oral iron products can interfere with the absorption of certain antibiotics and should not be taken within two hours of each other. Gastrointestinal discomfort, such as nausea, may occur but can be minimized by taking the product with meals. Iron-containing products may occasionally cause constipation or diarrhea. Pregnant or nursing individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using this product. Accidental overdose of iron-containing products is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under six years of age. Keep this product out of reach of children. In case of accidental overdose, contact a doctor or poison control center immediately. Adverse reactions to ferrous sulfate are not well-documented in clinical trials or post-marketing data. Similarly, there is limited information on drug interactions, pharmacology, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology. There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of ferrous sulfate during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing, or in pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial, renal-impaired, hepatic-impaired, or immunocompromised populations. Ferrous sulfate is administered orally, and there is limited information on its intravenous use or monitoring requirements. It should be stored at room temperature. Patients should be counseled on the potential effects of alcohol when taking this medication, as the interaction between alcohol and ferrous sulfate has not been established. The brand name for ferrous sulfate is Feosol®, and there is limited information on look-alike drug names. Finally, ferrous sulfate should be used with caution and under medical supervision to ensure safe and effective treatment of iron deficiency and related conditions.
